oldFifteen.note: the 15 known problems of v1-v3, inside the same runs; v3 had 7,4,5,5

smallestGain.method: Each known problem is found with its own rate p (found/3 here). One run total then varies with sd = sqrt(sum p(1-p)) = 1.41 bugs (the 3 totals 14, 13, 12 give sd 1.0). Comparing two variants with k runs each, the difference of their means has sd 1.41*sqrt(2/k); a gain counts at 95% confidence with 80% power when it is 2.8 times that.
smallestGain.answer: With 3 runs per variant, a gain of about 3 known problems (of 40, +8 points of recall) is real; 1 or 2 is still noise. The old 15-case set needed about +3 of 15 (+20 points) for the same.

verdict: Baseline for main 2ef1ad8 with Sonnet: 13 of 40 known problems per run (12 to 14), precision 0.90 (0.84 to 0.94), 1 false alarm on the 20 clean pull requests per run (0 to 2), a first-try finish_review refusal in 23% of reviews (10 to 16 of 60), a third of them invalid JSON the model sent. 9 known problems are found every time, 9 sometimes, 22 never. The never-found ones are mostly crashes on an input the diff does not show, typing breaks, side effects through getters or generators, concurrency and resource bugs.

cost.note: Three full runs were estimated at $41 after the first ($13.68), over the $40 cap, so the third run started with the 40 problem cases only; it cost less than expected and left room to run the 20 clean ones too, so all 60 got 3 runs.
